fix_commit_message:
avcodec/dxv: Check coded_height, to avoid invalid av_clip()

Fixes: assertion failure
Fixes: 438961582/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_DXV_DEC_fuzzer-5850827739955200

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix cdee519d40e6 on top of intro 2f9936e446d5 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): In libavcodec/dxv.c, the DXV decoder computes per-plane decompression thread slice counts using av_clip(avctx->thread_count, 1, coded_height / TEXTURE_BLOCK_H). When coded_height (or its halved value used for chroma planes in planar YCG6/YG10 formats) is small enough that integer division by TEXTURE_BLOCK_H (4) yields 0, av_clip() is invoked with a maximum bound (0) smaller than its minimum bound (1), violating the function's precondition and triggering an assertion failure (or, in release builds, producing an incoherent clip result) reachable from a crafted/fuzzed DXV bitstream. Root cause: The refactor that introduced texdsp_ctx-based slice_count computation (replacing the previous FFMAX(ctx->texture_block_h, ctx->ctexture_block_h) based divisor) did not add a guard ensuring the coded_height-derived divisor used in av_clip()'s max argument is >= 1 before calling av_clip(), allowing pathological small coded_height values from attacker-controlled input to violate av_clip()'s min<=max invariant.
